bounds.domain: One cancelled locate generation, one asynchronous cleanup receipt, at most one replacement locate or typed origin, and one accepted replacement fix.
limitations: The finite generation numbers abstract monotonically increasing source tickets. Native cleanup success or failure settles explicitly. Late old fix delivery cannot publish after cancellation. The model does not prove physical watch cleanup, native permission grants, cross-process events or unbounded replacement chains.

The actual-source test holds and rejects an old cleanup after the real controller accepts a newer fix. Existing screen tests cover search, typed origin, Start and timeout while an old fix is delayed. Conditional progress assumes native cleanup and local continuation settle, without assuming cleanup succeeds.

Only the retired cleanup receipt is projected. A cleanup failure owned by the current generation still surfaces as a current position error; the model does not assert that all current one-shot cleanup succeeds.

assumptions: No fairness. This projection includes no later explicit user replacement after the accepted fix.
Weak fairness of the native cleanup receipt, either success or failure, and its local continuation. This does not claim that a failed cleanup stopped the physical watch.
No fairness. An outstanding cleanup receipt may never settle.
